instructions: This file is one part of the interface of Forge Studio, an AI image and video app (Stable Diffusion WebUI Forge).
Translate every value in "texts" (and in "blocks", when there is one) into the language you were asked for. Never change a key: the program finds each text by its English key.
Fill in "language" with the language's own name (for example "Español"), "code" with its short code (for example "es" or "pt-br"), and set "direction" to "rtl" for a language written right to left.

Keep exactly as they are: {0}, {name} and other words in curly braces, %s, ${...}, HTML tags and their attributes, emoji, \n line breaks, numbers and units, keyboard keys, file names and paths, and code.

Keep the names of models, samplers, programs and formats in English (FLUX, SDXL, SD 1.5, LoRA, ControlNet, AnimateDiff, Deforum, Wan, VAE, CFG, Euler a, LCM, Hires. fix, PNG, MP4...). For a technical term the user will meet in English tutorials, add the English in brackets once, for example "Escala CFG (CFG Scale)".
Short labels stay short: they are buttons, tabs and field names. Use the plain, friendly words a video editor or a photo app uses in that language.
A value that should stay in English may stay unchanged.
Return the complete file as valid JSON with the same structure and nothing before or after it.

blocks.4_other_blocks#6:
To increase consistency it's better to inpaint clear objects on video with good quality and enough context. Your prompts need to produce consistent results

To suppress flickering you can generate in little fps (e.g. 10), then interpolate (x2) it with ai interpolation algorithm (e.g RIFE or frame interpolation in deforum sd-webui extension)

You can also use sd-webui-controlnet or lama-cleaner with (low denoising) extensions to increase consistency, if it fits to your scenario

Also a good can be to use Pass the previous frame into ControlNet with IP-Adapter, Reference, Shuffle, T2IA-Color, T2IA-Style
blocks.4_other_blocks#7: All detection options including prompt are taken from Replacer tab. You can stop masking at any time, and it will cut output video

1. Create your wildcard library by copying a collection using the dropdown in the Collection actions.
  2. Click on the files that appear in the tree to edit them.

blocks.5_settings_blocks#0:
<abbr title="Variational autoencoder">VAE</abbr> is a neural network that transforms a standard <abbr title="red/green/blue">RGB</abbr>
image into latent space representation and back. Latent space representation is what stable diffusion is working on during sampling
(i.e. when the progress bar is between empty and full). For txt2img, VAE is used to create a resulting image after the sampling is finished.
For img2img, VAE is used to process user's input image before the sampling, and to create an image after sampling.
blocks.5_settings_blocks#1:
This page allows you to change default values in UI elements on other tabs.
Make your changes, press 'View changes' to review the changed default values,
then press 'Apply' to write them to C:\ForgeStudio\forge\webui\ui-config.json.
New defaults will apply after you restart the UI.
blocks.9_manual_animatediff_blocks#0: Upload up to three things, write the prompt in the usual place and press Generate: Dance video: real people dancing. Only their movement is taken, not how they look. The dancers: pictures of what the dancers are made of (a water drop, glass, spaghetti). Close-ups of the material work best. In the prompt, describe them as the material: two figures made entirely of spaghetti, rather than two dancers. The background (optional): pictures of the place behind the dancers (a jungle, a beach, a stage). They give the background its atmosphere and colors; the picture itself is not copied. Without them the background comes only from the prompt. Pick a picture taken from the same angle as the dance video (a stage filmed from the side needs a side view; a picture from above turns the whole scene into a top view). A picture of the place without the dancers' material works best (a bowl with sauce on a table, not a bowl full of spaghetti), so the dancers stand out. When the dancers are small in the frame, keep the picture plain (an empty table and wall): objects in it get repeated around the empty space. Length, music, size and ControlNet are set automatically; the checkpoint is the usual one. Your own ControlNet units are switched off while this is on.
blocks.9_manual_audio_blocks#0: Tick a parameter to open its settings. Function is its own function of x, the loudness 0..1 of its band, like on the website: 1 + x^4 reacts mostly to peaks, x evenly; bass, mids, highs, t (frame) and sec work too. Quiet and Loud stretch it between the value at the quietest and at the loudest moment of the song (leave both empty for the function's own values). Smooth = frames to fall back after a hit, Min / Max = hard limits (empty = none). Switch (camera motions) turns the direction around: 10 every 10 frames, beats on the beats, beats 1.5 on beats at least 1.5 s apart, empty = never. The plot updates when you leave a changed field.
blocks.9_manual_audio_blocks#1: Pick a camera mode and press 🎬 Direct the camera: the mode splits the analysed song into parts and fills the camera rows above (which motions move, how fast with which band, and when they switch direction). Then press Apply to Deforum. Save keeps the ticked camera rows and the song-part pattern as a new mode. Learn reads the Motion tab, for example a video whose camera you liked, and saves its style as a mode for other songs.
blocks.9_manual_blocks#0: No interpolation will be used. Requires one model; A. Allows for format conversion and VAE baking.
blocks.9_manual_blocks#1: The difference between the last two models will be added to the first. Requires three models; A, B and C. The result is calculated as A + (B - C) * M
blocks.9_manual_extrasvideo_blocks#0: Upload a video and choose below what to do with its frames: Hires. fix, an upscaler, face restoration. Preview a frame renders the one frame at “Preview from second”, Preview a short part from there. Both are shown with a line to drag across the picture: the original on one side, the result on the other. After a click on the picture the mouse wheel zooms in, and dragging then moves it. Generate renders the whole video. The result is an MP4 with the original sound.RTX Video Super Resolution is made for video and is by far the fastest; for a video from a phone or the web, its (compressed video) version also cleans away the compression blocks. R-ESRGAN redraws more and takes a second or more a frame; at ×2, R-ESRGAN 2x+ is about three times faster than 4x+. DAT is only for a few seconds of video.
blocks.9_manual_extrasvideo_blocks#1: The picture, or every frame of the video, is enlarged with the upscaler and then drawn over by the loaded checkpoint: this is what adds sharpness and detail. The panel starts on the LCM setup: sampler LCM, 8 steps, CFG 1, and the LCM LoRA in Added to the prompt, which joins the prompt the picture or video was made with (or the one written here). Denoising strength is how much is drawn anew: 0.2 to 0.3 sharpens and keeps the picture; 0.5 adds much more, invents things that were not there, and in a video more of it flickers. As in Hires. fix, all the Hires steps are run, on every frame: fewer steps are faster. 0 steps, 0 CFG, seed -1 and “Use same sampler” take what it was made with. Every frame is a generation of its own at the new size, so try Preview a frame first.
